headline: Saskatchewan Launches 41-Kilometre Highway 2 Resurfacing Project Connecting Assiniboia Corridor
summary: Assiniboia Mayor Sharon Schauenberg detailed a major provincial resurfacing and culvert installation project across 41 kilometres of Highway 2, enhancing trade logistics and regional agricultural transport.
metaDescription: Assiniboia Mayor Sharon Schauenberg details 41km Highway 2 paving and drainage upgrades connecting southern Saskatchewan transit corridors.
tweet: Saskatchewan advances 41-kilometre Highway 2 repaving and culvert drainage project connecting the Assiniboia regional transit corridor.
body:
The Saskatchewan Ministry of Highways and municipal leadership in the Town of Assiniboia have initiated a substantial 41-kilometre resurfacing and infrastructure rehabilitation project along Highway 2, modernizing one of the primary commercial transportation arteries across southern Saskatchewan. The capital undertaking aims to enhance roadway durability, freight safety, and agricultural supply chain connectivity between the Highway 13 junction and the Ardill Access corridor.

Assiniboia Mayor Sharon Schauenberg emphasized that while the extensive construction zone involves temporary single-lane closures and pilot vehicle management, the long-term economic dividends for regional grain haulers, local businesses, and rural commuters are substantial. In addition to deep asphalt repaving, the project includes the installation and structural replacement of 12 major drainage culverts designed to prevent subgrade washout during spring runoff events.

The initiative represents the second major phase of infrastructure investment in the Assiniboia region, following a municipal-provincial partnership that rehabilitated Centre Street and local drainage networks in the town centre. Provincial transportation planners highlighted that the upgrades incorporate heavy-haul paving standards capable of accommodating expanding commercial truck volumes generated by regional agricultural processing facilities.

Municipal officials have advised travelers to utilize the Saskatchewan Highway Hotline to monitor construction timelines and pilot vehicle intervals as paving crews advance along the corridor through the late summer construction window.

headline: Lonoke Mayor Wayne McGee to Serve Four-Year Term Following County Election Ballot Review
summary: Lonoke Mayor Wayne McGee will remain in office for an additional four-year term following an administrative election filing determination regarding municipal ballot certifications in Lonoke County.
seoTitle: Lonoke Mayor Wayne McGee Term Determination | Choseno
metaDescription: Lonoke Mayor Wayne McGee to continue in executive office following county election commission ballot certification review.
tweet: Lonoke Mayor Wayne McGee confirmed to serve new four-year municipal term following election certification review in Arkansas.
body:
Municipal governance in the City of Lonoke has been clarified following county election administrative proceedings, confirming that incumbent Mayor Wayne McGee will continue leading the city's executive administration for a full four-year term. The certification review resolved procedural questions regarding municipal candidate ballot filings for the upcoming November general election.

Under Arkansas statutory election guidelines, when statutory municipal petition deadlines pass without certified qualifying opposing ballot petitions, municipal incumbents or unopposed candidates are officially recognized without requiring individual ballot placement, preserving municipal resources while ensuring continuity of municipal services. City administration confirmed that municipal budget preparations, utility infrastructure upgrades, and downtown drainage improvements will proceed on schedule.

Mayor McGee’s administration has focused on wastewater treatment facility modernizations, industrial park recruitment along the Interstate 40 corridor, and local municipal street paving programs. The resolution allows city departments to advance multi-year capital improvement plans without electoral transition disruptions.

Lonoke City Council members and community stakeholders noted that municipal administrative focus will now center on completing ongoing drainage mitigation studies and finalizing the city's upcoming fiscal year operating budget.
